2611.33262.abstract: AI models are increasingly being deployed at the edge. Since these models often require significant research and development to produce, are often deployed in potentially hostile environments, and downstream systems often rely on accurate data; protecting them from theft or manipulation is worthy of serious consideration. Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), which provide hardware-enforced separation of software execution, can protect model weights but impose strict resource constraints, making full-model execution impractical for large neural networks. We present Onnx2TEE, an automated, model-independent pipeline that partitions ONNX models across rich, trusted execution environments for non-sequential feed-forward networks using graph-aware segmentation to preserve computational dependencies while minimizing boundary communication and reducing TEE-induced inference latency. Evaluation on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin using an Arm TrustZone TEE demonstrates that model parameters can be highly concentrated in individual segments, supporting selective protection of parameter-dense model components. The evaluation further shows that the generated trusted app's memory requirements depend on both computation and intermediate tensor sizes.

2611.33257.title: One Token, Many Lessons: Sliding-Window Attention within Gated Delta Networks
2611.33257.abstract: Linear attention compresses historical context into a fixed-size recurrent state, reducing the computational and memory costs of long-sequence modeling. From the perspective of test-time regression (TTR), the state matrix can be viewed as an online-learned regression model, where keys and values serve as inputs and targets respectively, and queries are used to read from the model. From this perspective, the effectiveness of state learning depends not only on the update rule but also on how the key-value learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. While existing work has largely focused on how the state is updated and organized, we investigate how the learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. To this end, we propose Sliding-Window Gated DeltaNet (SWGDN), which replaces short convolutions in Delta-Rule linear attention with sliding-window attention to perform content-dependent local aggregation of projected queries, keys, and values. Our experiments show that SWGDN makes the key-value pairs used in consecutive updates more similar in both GDN2 and KDA. In SWGDN, carrying information from the same token across updates can help the recurrent state reinforce a previously learned association. The local mixing strategy can be incorporated into any Delta-Rule-based linear attention architecture without changing its state update equations or chunkwise parallel algorithms. We apply this strategy to two Delta-Rule variants, GDN2 and KDA, and experimental results demonstrate that SWGDN outperforms the original Delta-Rule baseline across multiple benchmarks.

2611.33254.title: Anti-AI in the Wild: From Toxic Discourse to Action
2611.33254.abstract: Online discussion of generative AI has become increasingly contentious, and communities devoted to supporting, opposing, or debating AI have emerged on social media. Some of these communities take anti-AI actions, such as deploying crawler tarpits and data-poisoning services to interfere with data collection and model training. Yet, the scope of these actions and their relationship to online discourse remain poorly understood. In this paper, we present the first measurement study of online conflict over generative AI, from toxic discourse to anti-AI actions. We collect 931,640 posts from 25 Reddit communities, label them with a large language model detector validated against human labels, identify 3,312 anti-AI actions, and trace the output of three deployed anti-AI tools. Our analysis reveals that 30.0% of posts in communities devoted to this conflict are toxic, compared to 4.4% in general AI communities. Anti-AI actions in these communities mainly target AI crawling or model training data, such as image cloaking and data poisoning. We further examine the implications of these anti-AI actions for AI training, by analyzing the text and code generated from deployed tools. Notably, 66.5% of the code samples generated by a data-poisoning service contain fabricated facts, misused APIs, or broken logic, yet 93.6% passes a public code-curation pipeline, close to the rate for real source code (95.0%). For crawler tarpit output, adding a period to the end of each paragraph increases the curation survival rate from 16.4% to 91.9%. We also find that crawler tarpit and data-poisoning output has already entered Common Crawl, a widely used public web archive, and that crawler tarpit output has also entered FineWeb, a released pretraining dataset. We hope our study can facilitate a better understanding of online conflict over generative AI and its implications for content moderation and AI training.

2611.33243.title: Beyond the Efficiency-Efficacy Dilemma: A Critical Analysis of Transferability in Adversarial Malware Detection
2611.33243.abstract: Machine Learning (ML) models are already being deployed at scale for malware detection. Therefore there is a pressing need to rigorously study adversarial robustness. To that end, we introduce the Adversarial AI Engine (AAIE): a platform for automated security stress-testing. We performed transfer attacks, via EMBER2018, against a Random Forest target. Counterintuitively, we found single-step FGSM to have the highest attack success rate (ASR) of 52.9% compared to iterative PGD with 45.2% (p < 0.002). Compared to iterative attacks which tend to overfit surrogate networks creating brittle perturbations, FGSM created more transferable examples. We benchmarked our attacks using ASR, transferability score, evasion rate, and resilience index. Through these metrics, proposed in concordance with emerging standards in AI governance, we expose shortcomings as our transferability scores peak at ~0.8 with constrained perturbations. We highlight the practical security implications of these findings and demonstrate AAIE for automated adversarial auditing.

2611.33242.title: CypherMAS: Benchmarking Routing Reliability in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
2611.33242.abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) distribute reasoning across specialized agents that must exchange messages and invoke tools reliably. Existing evaluations typically couple communication with open domain tasks, making it difficult to determine whether a failure arises from reasoning, malformed tool use, lost messages, or forgotten requests. Prior benchmarks do not isolate communication execution or measure routing redundancy against a known optimal path. We introduce CypherMAS, a synthetic benchmark that isolates communication and routing in fixed multi-agent graphs. Agents in chain, star, bipartite, or ring graphs route cyphered messages to remote peers holding the matching decoders; since the optimal route is known, redundant LLM calls can be measured and routing failures may be easily tracked. Across eleven open-weight models from 4B to 753B, small models fail at routing and tool use, dense models above 27B degrade with diameter, and successful runs exceed minimum LLM calls. These findings identify communication reliability as a distinct scaling bottleneck for multi-agent systems and provide a controlled diagnostic for complex multi-agent systems. The source code is freely available: https://github.com/Andoree/CypherMAS.

2611.33238.title: Sequential Testing on Complex and High Dimensional Data Streams Leveraging Unsupervised Model Errors
2611.33238.abstract: We propose two general, distribution-free test statistics for binary Sequential Hypothesis Testing (SHT) and Sequential Change Point Detection (SCPD) respectively, in streaming environments where the data (e.g., network traffic metadata) are too complicated for the exact probabilistic modeling required by conventional likelihood ratio-driven tests. Our framework also addresses the challenge of information asymmetry, where data is available only from the null/pre-change regime and not from the alternative/post-change one such as zero-day attacks or emerging disease related regimes. The proposed statistics monitor the errors of a predictive or reconstructive machine learning model trained solely on null/pre-change data, relying on imperfect generalization (the model's performance will degrade when deployed on data from the alternative/post-change class). Under mild assumptions on the model's errors, we establish rigorous analytical guarantees: strict non-asymptotic error control for SHT, and explicit bounds on the Average Run Length (ARL) and the Expected Detection Delay (EDD) for SCPD. Extensive evaluations in target tracking, chaotic dynamical systems, and real-world network security datasets, demonstrate that our framework consistently satisfies prescribed constraints where existing algorithms succumb to inflated missed detections and/or false alarms. Finally, because our methods operate on scalar errors without requiring online retraining or kernel evaluations, they are highly scalable.

2611.33236.title: KiRA: Kronecker Input-Gated Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models
2611.33236.abstract: Full fine-tuning of large pretrained models is expensive, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) is the standard alternative. Most PEFT methods use low-rank updates, whose rank lies far below that of full fine-tuning and is the same for every input. Input-adaptive variants vary the capacity per input but remain within the low-rank bottleneck, and whether a task benefits from input conditioning is not known before training. This paper introduces Kronecker input-gated rank adaptation (KiRA). Instead of the conventional low-rank product, the update $\Delta W$ is the Kronecker product of a frozen random $p\times p$ matrix $A$ and a trainable factor $M(x)$, which overcomes the rank ceiling: because rank is multiplicative under this product, $A$ multiplies the rank of $M(x)$ by $p$ without adding trainable parameters. The factor $M(x)$ is further decomposed as $B_1\,\mathrm{diag}(g(x))\,B_2$, where the input gate $g(x)$, computed once per sample by a network shared across all adapted layers, adjusts the rank of the update to each input in steps of $p$. Where input conditioning is unnecessary, the gate is folded into $B_1$ at deployment. Because the gate changes the rank only in discrete steps, the benefit of input conditioning can be predicted before training from a few hundred labeled inputs. Across six medical imaging and language benchmarks, KiRA attains the highest mean score against five published baselines with 8.7--9.7 times fewer trainable parameters than low-rank adaptation, and the pre-training criterion agrees with the measured benefit of input conditioning on all six tasks.

2611.33234.title: Diagnostically Meaningful, Privacy-aware Synthetic Chest CT via Class-Conditional Latent Sampling in Diffusion Autoencoders
2611.33234.abstract: Large, well-annotated datasets are essential for developing medical artificial intelligence models, yet data sharing is often restricted by privacy regulations. Synthetic images may help address this limitation if they preserve diagnostic information while reducing the risk of reproducing patient data. We developed a diffusion autoencoder-based framework for class-conditional synthetic chest CT generation that incorporates latent-space distance filtering to reduce the likelihood of regenerating training samples. A diffusion autoencoder was trained on the public RSNA 2020 Pulmonary Embolism (PE) dataset. PE-positive and PE-negative images were synthesized by sampling latent representations from class-specific kernel density estimates. Samples with a nearest-neighbor latent-space distance below a predefined threshold were rejected. To assess diagnostic utility, ResNet-50 classifiers were trained across 10 independent runs using real, synthetic, or mixed real-synthetic datasets. Performance was evaluated on a held-out real test set using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), with DeLong 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Models trained on synthetic data achieved an AUC of 0.862 (95% CI, 0.851-0.874), only slightly lower than models trained on real data (AUC = 0.872, 95% CI, 0.861-0.883) and mixed real-synthetic data (AUC = 0.865, 95% CI, 0.855-0.876). These differences were statistically significant (p < 0.05) but small in absolute terms. A nearest-neighbor copy-detection analysis of 38,000 synthetic slices found no direct copies of real training images. These findings indicate that the synthetic CT images preserve diagnostically meaningful information for image-level PE classification while incorporating measures intended to enhance privacy awareness and reduce similarity to real patient data.

2611.33201.title: The AI Disclosure Paradox: Operational Disclosure and the Rise of Corporate AI Narratives
2611.33201.abstract: AI-related corporate disclosure can expand while becoming less concentrated on current use. Across U.S. SEC filings from 2017 to 2025, AI-related passage intensity increased 6.3-fold between 2017-2022 and 2023-2025, whereas corrected operational-disclosure intensity increased 3.3-fold. The operational share fell from 25.76% to 13.45%; approximately 89% of the net increase in passage intensity fell outside the operational category. The decline persists within sectors and filing types and in 10-K-only analysis. These estimates combine frozen language-model predictions for 26,279 AI-related passages with an audit of 1,000 annotated passages. The findings distinguish growth in organizational attention from growth in implementation-specific claims: more operational disclosure can coexist with a substantially lower operational share. Operational disclosure was thus diluted, not displaced, by nonoperational disclosure. Reading corporate technology narratives therefore requires attention to both disclosure intensity and the organizational state described.

2611.33198.title: UniMoE-CP: Unified Conditional Waveform Prediction Across Measured Optical Wireless Links
2611.33198.abstract: Shared prediction across measured optical wireless links requires a common model to accommodate link-dependent waveform dynamics. This paper studies unified learning for underwater optical, 100-m visible-light communication and 4.3-km free-space optical links. We formulate received-waveform forecasting from historical observations and known future transmitted excitation using one shared parameter set. UniMoE-CP combines a shared pool of temporal experts, window-dependent routing and spectral covariate fusion with an autoregressive decoder. The design permits conditional specialization while reusing expert parameters across the measured links. Pooled-training benchmarks evaluate each link separately and report an aggregated result using normalized mean square error (NMSE) and normalized mean absolute error (NMAE). The reported average NMSE reductions are 29.9% for 100-m VLC, 29.1% underwater and 21.4% for 4.3-km FSO. The aggregated average NMSE decreases from 0.1645 for the best baseline to 0.1178 for UniMoE-CP.

2611.33197.title: Extraneous Cognitive Load in Large Language Models
2611.33197.abstract: Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) shows that human problem-solving is affected by both intrinsic load, arising from task difficulty, and extraneous load, arising from how task information is presented. Large language models (LLMs) show analogous effects: presentation alone can affect model performance, but these effects have not yet been systematically isolated from task difficulty. To address this gap, we introduce CogLoadBench, a controlled benchmark that varies five CLT-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families. Across models, we find that higher extraneous load conditions often reduce accuracy by either adding competition or complicating the reasoning path. To support diagnosis and mitigation of load-related effects, we propose the Extraneous Load Score (ELS), a prompt-time metric computed from activations that estimates a model's extraneous load, and show that it generalizes across reasoning task types and load levels. We further show that shifting model representations toward lower-load directions at inference time can improve average model performance without changing prompt content.

2611.33195.title: Verified experience improves materials prediction with large language models
2611.33195.abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. We present MatRecall, a framework that lets large language models store verified predictions, with evidence, outcome and error, as episodes and recall them without retraining. MatRecall improved median performance by 62% over a memory-free model, exceeded specialized models on 11 tasks, remained useful after feedback stopped and transferred between related tasks. Verified experience could become a reusable resource for self-improving discovery loops.

2611.33193.title: Formalization, Transparency, and Collusion in Open-Source Game Theory
2611.33193.abstract: Cooperation among AI agents will undermine alignment protocols when it takes the form of collusion. Under these protocols, agents often have some information about one another, and how much they have may determine whether they collude. Open-source game theory studies the extreme case, in which each program reads its opponent's source code and acts based on what it can prove about it. We develop formal foundations for this theory: we specify a concrete proof system, resolve an open problem concerning DupocBot and CupodBot through a transposition argument, and mechanize the framework in Lean 4; to our knowledge, this is the first mechanization of resource-bounded open-source game theory. We then extend the framework to the more realistic setting of partial transparency, where each program receives only partial information about its opponent. In Prisoner's Dilemma experiments, where mutual cooperation models collusion, greater transparency increases both the cooperation sustainable in equilibrium and the cooperation selected by replicator dynamics. This suggests that controlling how much agents can know about one another matters for alignment protocols.

2611.33184.title: Semantic Density Does Not Predict Agent-Memory Collapse
2611.33184.abstract: Persistent textual memory can improve LLM agents, but repeated updates can erode task performance. We ask whether memory-store statistics warn before held-out accuracy declines. We registered mean pairwise cosine similarity ($\rho$) and 13 additional geometry, retrieval, and graph statistics on 805 snapshots from 13 memory methods across ALFWorld, AppWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, and two ARC-AGI settings. These methods store trajectories, rules, workflows, strategies, or linked records, using selective retrieval or whole-store prompting. No such statistic reliably predicted early signs of task accuracy decline, and $\rho$ had zero median lead. With the checkpoint after peak accuracy as a secondary decline point, measures of highly similar pairs and nearest-neighbor crowding changed earlier but did not consistently outperform stored-item count. We trained classifiers on this corpus and applied them unchanged to PropWorld runs of up to 5,000 crafting tasks. They falsely flagged 56.9% of checkpoints from size-limited stores with stable accuracy and detected only 18% of checkpoints after task success fell to zero. Thus, global semantic density did not provide a reliable warning, while local crowding did not transfer consistently across memory designs. In these long-horizon runs, size-limited stores remained stable, while the sole failure arose when unbounded whole-store prompting exceeded model input capacity, which token growth predicted directly.

2611.33183.title: REI: Learning Ideation from Repository Evolution
2611.33183.abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable of executing and evaluating experiments, ideation is emerging as a bottleneck in automated scientific and engineering iteration. In many real-world domains, useful ideas are sparse and their validation is costly, making direct online exploration inefficient. We observe that repository evolution provides a scalable source of reusable technical experience: code changes record concrete technical hypotheses, while subsequent revisions, adoption, and reuse provide signals about their utility. Based on this observation, we propose REI, a Repository Evolution-driven Ideation framework that learns reusable ideation policies from repository evolution, injecting domain-specific technical experience into model parameters and reducing reliance on costly trial-and-error. We further identify a hidden failure mode in quality-driven ideation optimization: semantic diversity collapse. Although generated ideas can remain lexically diverse, they increasingly concentrate in a small number of dominant method families, limiting cross-task generalization and long-tail exploration. To address this problem, we introduce Semantic Prior Optimization and Debiasing (SPOD), a diversity-preserving alignment mechanism that makes method identity explicit, corrects category-level reward bias, and limits redundant accumulation within the same method family while retaining strong representatives. Experiments on public benchmarks and a real-world industrial setting demonstrate improvements in ideation quality, method diversity, cross-task generalization, and long-tail exploration.

2611.33182.title: Neighbor Crowding Predicts Feature Stability in Sparse Autoencoders
2611.33182.abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) offer an approach to identify language model representations by breaking apart polysemantic features into more sparse, interpretable ones. Yet, it is challenging to identify which of the learned features are actually stable, rather than artifacts of initialization. One approach is to train multiple SAE seeds, and compare the learned features across seeds by cosine similarity, but this is notably costly. This raises the question of whether stable features can be identified without the computational expense of training multiple seeds. In this work, we examine cross-seed feature stability across differing levels of training tokens, and demonstrate that in TopK SAEs, it is highly predictable using six computationally cheap statistics derived from a single training run. Neighbor crowding, a geometric property of the dictionary, is the strongest single predictor, with features that sit in dense regions of the unit sphere more likely to be stable than isolated ones.

2611.33176.title: Psychophysics of Duration Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
2611.33176.abstract: Studies of time perception in language models focus mainly on text-based settings. Yet multimodal models are increasingly used for tasks that require perceiving the passage of time, making the limits of their temporal perception important to understand. We measure the limits of duration perception from audio against a human baseline to address this gap. Drawing from psychophysics, we operationalise duration perception as a melody recognition task, testing when a melody becomes unrecognisable as it is slowed down. Of 21 tested models, most cannot recognise well-known melodies without labelled in-context examples. With in-context examples, seven recognise melodies reliably, most peaking within the median human recognition band. Generalisation is limited: (i) recognition peaks shift with in-context example speed, (ii) melody titles induce prediction bias, and (iii) providing examples with scientific pitch notation does not prevent accuracy declining at long note durations for most models. In humans, the recognition window is a property of the perceiver; in current models, it is largely a property of the prompt.

2611.24990.title: Show Your Work: Can Small Open Models Read SEC Filings with Evidence a Machine Can Check?
2611.24990.abstract: A fluent answer from a language model is not a verified one. We ask whether small open models that run on a single consumer GPU can extract numbers from SEC filings with evidence a machine can check: the page and a verbatim quote containing the number. We introduce Filing-Evidence, a benchmark of 1,000 questions over 90 recent 10-K and 10-Q filings of 45 US companies, with answer keys taken from the filers' inline XBRL tags. We evaluate ten instruct models from ten developers (7-21B parameters) on one RTX 4090 in three setups: plain, check-and-retry, and the model's own reasoning mode. Accuracy with checkable evidence ranges from 17.1% to 82.7% in the plain setup, and the best result is 84.5% (Qwen3.5-9B). An automatic checker rejects many wrong answers, but between 16 and 167 answers per 1,000 give a wrong value for an answerable question and still pass every check. In the plain setup, 57% of these are scale or unit errors and 30% take another period or column of the right line. Reasoning significantly reduces such errors for 4 of 5 models that offer it. Retrying after a failed check raises accuracy by up to 3.9 points but never reduces them. Questions, model outputs, code and protocol are public.

2611.33786.title: Evaluating Cine and Tagged MRI-to-Speech Synthesis with Complementary Metrics and MRI-Free Controls
2611.33786.abstract: Relating tongue motion measured with dynamic MRI to the speech it produces could inform rehabilitation after glossectomy. Prior studies have translated cine or tagged MRI into log-mel spectrograms and used the two-dimensional Pearson correlation between predicted and recorded spectrograms (Corr2D) to quantify the acoustic information captured by each imaging modality. However, Corr2D has not been calibrated against MRI-free predictors that preserve basic acoustic structure. Our contribution is an evaluation framework for speech synthesis from cine MRI, tagged MRI and their combination; the synthesis network is held fixed. On identical leave-one-subject-out folds, we compare four trained input configurations with two MRI-free controls: a static mean-spectrum baseline and a time-aligned cohort template. Across 44 subjects (18 after glossectomy) producing two utterances, the cohort template, which never sees an MRI, reached a Corr2D of 0.745 and 0.664. The static baseline, which contains no timing, reached 87 to 89% of that score. No trained configuration outperformed the template on Corr2D, a cepstral distance or ESTOI; seven of the eight fell significantly short on Corr2D. For cine MRI this held across three positional encodings, an encoder temporal-attention module and a training objective matched to the metric. Cine and tagged MRI differed consistently within subjects, although the direction depended on the metric. Absolute Corr2D alone therefore does not show that a model recovers acoustics from the MRI. The two controls are a reusable method: any study can compute them from its own training recordings, so a model's margin over them measures what its images contribute.

2611.33626.title: PICE: Prototype-Informed Conditional Model Evolution Toward Self-Evolving Medical Image Recognition
2611.33626.abstract: Medical image classifiers in clinical practice must continually evolve to accommodate emerging disease categories while maintaining reliable classification of existing conditions. This is challenging because privacy and data-sharing restrictions limit access to historical patient data, while assigning dedicated capacity to each new diagnostic task causes linear model growth. Effective evolution requires preserving prior disease knowledge without retaining historical images while expanding model capacity only when necessary. To this end, we propose PICE, a Prototype-Informed Conditional Model Evolution framework organized around what to preserve, when evolution is needed, and how that evolution is realized. PICE preserves prior disease knowledge in a prototype-statistical memory. For each incoming task, it assesses compatibility with historical references reconstructed from memory, reusing the closest adapter when compatibility is sufficient and instantiating a new one when evolution is required. PICE then realizes evolution by updating the memory and recalibrating the unified classifier with Gaussian pseudo features, thereby integrating new knowledge into the cumulative diagnostic space. During inference, memory-derived similarities guide task-agnostic adapter selection and fusion, enabling prediction over all learned disease categories. Experiments on Skin8, Kvasir-V2, and Path16 demonstrate the effectiveness of PICE across diverse clinical scenarios. On Skin8, PICE achieves a 7.60\% improvement in accuracy over the SOTA method on new tasks, while maintaining 71.10\% accuracy on previous tasks. It also reduces additional learnable parameters by 18.51\%. These results indicate that PICE improves classification while balancing knowledge retention, adaptation, and parameter growth, supporting continual model evolution as new diagnostic categories emerge without access to historical images.

2611.33235.title: Conformal Risk Control for Sentinel-1 Flood Maps under Event Shift and Local Recalibration
2611.33235.abstract: Conformal Risk Control (CRC) selects a threshold to limit missed labeled positives under exchangeability, but low omission risk can come at the cost of an excessively large flood map. We examine this trade-off with a frozen bi-temporal Sentinel-1 predictor, 403 expert-labeled source groups, and ten evaluable leave-one-event-out folds. At a target risk of 0.10, source-calibrated thresholds produce mean group losses of 0.1726 in Somalia and 0.1985 in Nigeria (four groups). The other eight folds select zero thresholds, labeling every valid pixel as flooded; their excess predicted area is 3.15-20.55 times the labeled positive area. Local threshold recalibration is feasible in 559 of 570 scheduled splits. The equal-event frequency of meeting the observed risk target with a positive threshold is 0.95% at ten labeled groups and 8.00% at twenty, using different predefined event pools. At fifty groups, exploratory recalibration meets both conditions in 24/30 Paraguay splits and none in India or the United States. Labels include permanent water, so the loss does not isolate newly flooded land. The results show why omission risk should be reported alongside mapped area, calibration feasibility, and event-specific outcomes.

2611.33194.title: Partitioning and Merging in Phase Unwrapping: A Systematic Review of Methods and Evidence
2611.33194.abstract: Phase unwrapping underlies radar interferometry, magnetic resonance imaging and optical metrology. When an image is too large or too difficult to unwrap in one piece, many methods cut it into units, unwrap each unit, and merge the results. To our knowledge, no systematic review had brought these partitioned methods together. This review gathers them, for two-dimensional images and three-dimensional volumes. It describes how the units are built: fixed tiles, adaptive tiles, regions computed from the data, or pieces imposed by the acquisition, such as subapertures, slices and scenes. It then classifies how the units are merged, in four classes: after each unit is unwrapped, through one integer per jump-free region, during the solve, or through an external reference. Three findings stand out: building the units and merging them are two separate decisions; the merging rule decides whether the merged phase stays congruent with the measured one; and most tests change both decisions at once, so few results show which one helps. We state what a study can report to support a claim on memory, speed or accuracy. Our aim is to document the methods, not to rank them. Following PRISMA 2020, four bibliographic databases (OpenAlex, IEEE Xplore, Web of Science and Scopus), searched on 1 October 2026, returned 1,800 records. After removing duplicates, screening titles and abstracts, adding a citation search and reading 298 full texts, we included 149 studies, published from 1987 to 2026. The review was not registered and received no specific funding.

2611.33686.title: From Entropy Source to Stochastic Bit-Stream: Low-Cost Converters for True-Random Stochastic Computing
2611.33686.abstract: Stochastic computing (SC) encodes values as the probability of ones in random bit-streams, which allows arithmetic circuits with very low area and power and a natural tolerance to faults. The accuracy and security of an SC system depend on the quality of those bit-streams. Conventional generators build them from pseudo-random or quasi-random sequences, which are predictable, periodic, and correlated across streams drawn from the same generator. This work proposes three methods for converting the unbiased outputs of a true random number generator (TRNG) into stochastic bit-streams (SBS) with arbitrary target probabilities: a block extraction and comparison circuit, a counter-logic circuit, and a cascaded majority-logic pipeline. All three accept bits from any true- random source and are built from standard CMOS logic. They reach the accuracy of a software random generator for both independent and correlated stream generation, and they support the common SC arithmetic operations with error that falls with stream length at the same rate. Hardware synthesis results show that the converters offer favorable area, energy, and area-delay trade-offs relative to pseudo- and quasi-random baselines. Under injected soft errors, block extraction degrades no faster than the best deterministic baseline. By bridging raw entropy sources and application-ready bit-streams, this work makes true-random SC practical on standard CMOS.

2611.28905.title: Beyond the section plane: Robust 3D reconstruction of multiplex immunofluorescence exposes limitations of 2D spatial cell statistics
2611.28905.abstract: Spatial analysis of the tumour microenvironment with multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) typically relies on single thin tissue sections, which misrepresent the 3D tissue organisation and bias spatial cell statistics in ways that remain largely unquantified. We reconstruct 24 breast and lung tumour tissue microarray cores in 3D, each from 15-20 serial mIF sections, and compare spatial cell statistics in 3D with those from individual sections. Our pipeline combines affine pre-alignment with dense deformable refinement using RoMa v2, achieving a median target registration error of 1.79 $\mu$m, well below nuclear size, which allows nuclei to be linked across sections. While cell-type proportions are preserved in 2D (Pearson corr. $r \geq 0.99$), 3D analysis reveals up to 3.8 times shorter nearest-neighbour distances, 13-19% higher neighbourhood entropy, and 2-4 times more contacts per cell. Tissue composition can thus be reliably estimated from individual sections, whereas cell-cell interactions require volumetric analysis.
2611.28905.why: 多重免疫荧光组织 3D 重建（病理学）

2611.33303.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data
2611.33303.abstract: Procedurally generated logic problems are used to both evaluate and train reasoning in language models. Their difficulty is usually set by planting a proof, that is, by sampling a proof of the desired depth and stating its premises as the problem. However, a planted proof is only one possible proof. A problem can also have shorter proofs, or several unrelated ones, and its stated depth then overstates what solving it requires. We measure what a problem actually requires, relative to a stated set of inference rules. For each problem, we compute the steps every proof must make, the shortest proof, the number of minimal proofs and the indispensable premises, and export certificates that an independent checker verifies. Audits of eight datasets find depth that is forced (ProofWriter, Blocksworld), problems labelled depth 5 that require about two specific rule applications (FLDx2), and answers that need no particular step (ZebraLogic). We then construct problems whose every proof has a requested structure, using a catalog of shortcuts proved once per rule set. Every constructed problem is checked in full and comes with its own certificate. In training, the best data mixes depths and problem types. At equal size, such mixtures of certified problem types, including model-checking problems that forward generation does not produce, transfer better than FLDx2-style derivation data for Qwen3 models from 0.6B to 8B.
2611.33303.why: LLM 逻辑推理难度校准

2611.33352.title: Why Does Sensor Depth Fail Learned Manipulation Policies? Finding the Failure Mode with ACT
2611.33352.abstract: Learned manipulation policies, from task-specific imitation policies to vision-language-action (VLA) models, rely primarily on RGB images. While some studies report gains from sensor depth, others avoid depth cameras because of measurement noise. Depth cameras introduce both noise and missing depth values (holes), whose relative effects remain unclear. In this study, we calibrate a sensor model using a real wrist-mounted stereo camera and separately evaluate noise and holes on RGB-D imitation policies with three visual encoders in simulation. We found that complete depth improves success by approximately ten percentage points, and most of this gain persists even at twenty times the camera's noise level. In contrast, holes covering about one-sixth of the wrist image eliminate the detectable benefit of depth. The validity mask strongly influences depth reliance: marking a small fraction of pixels as invalid reduces reliance, while filling holes and marking them valid restores most of the benefit. Policies trained on clean depth also lose performance when holes appear only at deployment, sometimes falling below RGB-only performance. These findings suggest that depth cameras for learned policies should therefore be judged by depth coverage more than measurement precision.
2611.33352.why: 机械臂操作中的深度传感器失效分析

2611.33380.title: FOCI: Trajectory Optimization on Gaussian Splats for Gaussian Robots
2611.33380.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has recently gained popularity as a faster alternative to Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) in 3D reconstruction and view synthesis methods. Leveraging the spatial information encoded in 3DGS, this work proposes FOCI (Field Overlap Collision Integral), an algorithm that is able to optimize trajectories directly on the Gaussians themselves. FOCI leverages a novel and interpretable collision formulation for 3DGS using the notion of the overlap integral between Gaussians. The formulation presented applies to different robot morphologies (e.g., fixed and mobile base manipulators, legged robots, UAVs) and handles both static and dynamic Gaussian-Splat environments. Contrary to other approaches, which represent the robot with conservative bounding boxes that underestimate the traversability of the environment, we propose to represent the environment and the robot as Gaussian Splats. This not only has desirable computational properties, but also allows for orientation-aware planning, allowing the robot to pass through very tight and narrow spaces. We extensively test our algorithm in both synthetic and real Gaussian Splats, showcasing that collision-free trajectories for legged, aerial and manipulator robots can be computed in seconds, even with hundreds of thousands of Gaussians making up the environment. The code is available at https://github.com/leggedrobotics/foci
2611.33380.why: 机器人轨迹优化（3DGS 仅作碰撞场）

2611.33390.title: RoboARC: Physical Puzzles for Robotic Manipulation under Spatial Constraints
2611.33390.abstract: Many hard manipulation tasks come down to a spatial constraint that only a few motions satisfy, such as passing a part through a gap barely wider than itself or separating two interlocked parts. These motions depend on the exact geometry of each scene, so demonstrations and skills recorded elsewhere rarely transfer. We therefore ask: when manipulation hinges on spatial constraints, can robots reason out the right motions? We introduce RoboARC, a benchmark of 90 tasks in six constraint types over rigid and soft materials, on three robots in MuJoCo. Every task is a frozen scene with a physics-based grader and a verified reference solution that replays bit-identically. Each task comes in a Privileged regime, with the full simulator state and resets, and a Standard regime with real-sensor inputs (camera images and proprioception) and a single attempt without resets. We evaluate seven coding agents and four VLA policies, none trained on these tasks. The strongest agent, GPT-6 Astra in Codex, solves 86% of the tasks in the Privileged regime and 43% in the Standard regime, and the four VLA policies, run zero-shot, solve none of their 18 one-arm puzzles. On 15 puzzles that GPT-6 Astra solved in the Privileged regime and failed in the Standard regime, object poses add 4 points and part geometry 13, but both together add 36, from 24% to 60%. Only 7% of the coding agents' failed runs pass more than half of a task, and 53% of the failed runs in the Standard regime are stuck on a single step. Frontier coding agents already reason out the right motions for many of these tasks once they know where the parts are and what shape they have. From their own sensors, in a single attempt, the strongest solves fewer than half of the tasks. The website can be found at https://roboarc.embodied-first-exam.ai
2611.33390.why: 机器人空间约束操作谜题

2611.33428.title: When the Knowledge Runs Out: A Part-Level Pilot Evaluation of How Language Models Handle Partially Covered Questions
2611.33428.abstract: Assistants that answer from supplied reference material often receive material that covers some parts of a user's question and not others. Existing evaluations of insufficient context mostly score one answer per question, and often treat partially sufficient context as simply insufficient. We describe a small, open evaluation that scores each part of a three-part question separately, with a verdict for parts that are answered correctly from the material but carry an added unsupported claim. On 30 cases (five scenarios, six coverage patterns, five samples each) we test claude-haiku-4-5 and llama3.1:8b. Without an explicit instruction to stay within the material, both models fill most gaps from their own knowledge (unsupported-claim rates of 0.71 and 0.90). One added sentence instructing them to answer only from the material brings these rates to 0.00 and 0.06, consistent with prior work. What remains is less visible: answers that strengthen the material, for example turning "many job sites prohibit bots" into a flat "no". We also report on the judge. Three rounds of blind hand labelling show that this added-claim verdict is the hardest to apply, for the judge and the author alike; RAGAS faithfulness is unsuitable for this task because it penalises correct withholding; and a difference between the two models that is clear under one judge disappears when the judge model is replaced. The dataset, code, hand labels and per-run figures are public.
2611.33428.why: 语言模型部分覆盖问答评测

2611.33460.title: Fast Muscle-Driven Whole-Body Motion Tracking with a Differentiable World Model
2611.33460.abstract: Tracking motion capture with a whole-body musculoskeletal model means coordinating hundreds of muscles through contact, and current controllers take hours to days of GPU time to train, so every tuning decision is expensive. SuperMimic trains a tracking policy by backpropagating through the rollouts of a learned world model. We extend it to MS-Human-700 (700 muscles) and MyoFullBody (354 muscles), with MuJoCo's activation dynamics inside the world model. To make its training fast, our recipe takes the speedups developed for the Unitree G1, replaces three of their settings that fail on muscles, and adds four changes of our own: observations without muscle geometry, data collection concurrent with the updates, Beta exploration noise that keeps every excitation in $[0,1]$, and 50 Hz control. On one RTX 5090 it trains MS-Human-700 in 6.3 minutes to the held-out return that SuperMimic's published hyperparameters reach in 3.9 hours, 37$\times$ sooner, and in 20 minutes to lower tracking errors than theirs after 10 hours. It trains MyoFullBody 34$\times$ sooner without retuning. Ablations show what is specific to muscles: a higher policy learning rate stalls half of the runs, and clipped Gaussian noise adds a tonic co-contraction that Beta noise avoids. Finally, refining the policy's actions through the world model at test time lowers the position error by a further 26% with no held-out clip failing, and reaches the same return after 5.1 instead of 6.3 minutes of training. Code, the training recipe and videos are on the project page https://muscle-supermimic.beanpow.top.
2611.33460.why: 肌骨模型全身动作跟踪（生物力学）

2611.33498.title: A 3D Simulator for Passive SPAD Imaging
2611.33498.abstract: Passive single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) cameras provide short-exposure observations for low-light perception, but collecting task annotations for these sensors remains difficult, and annotated datasets are scarce. We present a 3D simulation pipeline that generates realistic photon detections together with camera-motion and semantic labels, enabling perception models to be trained on synthetic SPAD observations and applied directly to real-world data. The pipeline couples controllable scene geometry and motion with a sensor-informed observation model that accounts for photon shot noise, dark counts, and spatial crosstalk. We evaluate the pipeline through calibrated photon-count comparisons and zero-shot sim-to-real transfer across three downstream perception tasks. We show that classifiers trained only on synthetic SPAD data achieve high accuracy on real low-light recordings at illumination levels less than 2 lux, without real-data fine-tuning. Similarly, we apply models trained entirely on simulated camera sweeps to real-world camera-rotation estimation and achieve mean absolute rotation errors of less than 1 degree on real 20-degree and 30-degree sweeps at 0.5 and 5.0 lux, when deployed zero-shot. We additionally train semantic segmentation models on synthetic data with automatically generated dense labels and perform direct inference on real-world low-light recordings; the results further demonstrate the usefulness of synthetic dense supervision for real low-light perception. Our simulator thus provides a practical source of annotated training data for real SPAD perception.
2611.33498.why: 被动 SPAD 成像仿真（通用低光感知）

2611.33567.title: ProPolar: Progressive Polar Decomposition for Implicit Neural Representations
2611.33567.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) capture global low-frequency structure during the early stage of training and then refine localized high-frequency details, afterwards. However, standard optimizers are agnostic to the coarse-to-fine learning behavior of INRs. Such optimizers accumulate a gradient matrix in momentum buffer and retain components misaligned with the dominant low-frequency directions in the early stage. We propose a progressively growing rank scheduler and a rank-aware learning-rate scheduler for enhancing a subspace-based momentum optimization, where a momentum matrix is updated within a low-rank subspace. The rank schedule expands the subspace during training, and the scheduler holds the peak learning rate through rank growth so that the added subspace contributes to fine-detail recovery. Experiments on image fitting, single-image super-resolution (SISR), and neural radiance field optimization show that the proposed method improves convergence and peak reconstruction quality over competitive optimizers. The largest gains appear in the high-frequency refinement stage, mirroring the coarse-to-fine progression that the rank schedule targets. A significant study on hyperparameter optimization (HPO) on NeRF further confirms that these gains persist under matched search budgets.
2611.33567.why: 隐式神经表示优化器（通用 INR）

2611.33579.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
2611.33579.abstract: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. We present DexEngine, a simulation pipeline that turns human manipulation data into train-ready, physically executable arm-hand trajectories. DexEngine first places each clip's hand-object motion where the arms can reach it, finds an arm motion that follows the human hands, and then corrects the motion in physics simulation with residual reinforcement learning. From nine human hand-object datasets, we generate about 5,200 clips for each of four dexterous hands, augmented into 65,000 trajectories (116 h) and 325,000 episodes (578 h) in total. Even with arms attached, DexEngine tracks objects more accurately than prior floating-hand methods and runs over 10x faster than RL-based ones. Policies trained on our data far outperform those trained on the same clips without physics correction or with the arms attached after a floating-hand correction, showing that fine-tuning data need physics correction. Mid-training on our data further improves them at equal fine-tuning budget, in simulation and on a real robot.
2611.33579.why: 人手演示转机器人数据

2611.33705.title: Lab2Sim: Agentic Generation of Interactive Laboratory Equipment from Operation Videos
2611.33705.abstract: Generating laboratory assets that faithfully reproduce the appearance, structure, and joint motions of real equipment remains challenging. Existing asset generation methods struggle to directly generate simulation assets for all equipment observed in operation videos and to faithfully reproduce the appearance, joint motions, and internal cavities of the real equipment. To address the challenge, we present Lab2Sim, an agentic framework that generates editable, simulation-ready laboratory equipment assets from egocentric or multi-view operation videos. Lab2Sim comprises four specialized agents. The Evidence Agent combines video observations with laboratory knowledge to specify equipment parts, materials, and functional requirements, which guide the Asset Agent in constructing editable Blender assets. The independent Verifier checks the generated geometry and appearance against the evidence and requirements, providing targeted feedback for revision. The Simulation Integration Agent converts verified Blender assets into simulation instances with physical properties and articulated mechanisms, using execution feedback to refine their behavior. Experiments on human and robot laboratory scenes show that Lab2Sim achieves higher visual fidelity and stronger interaction capability than coding-agent and real-to-sim baselines, including a Codex baseline using the same underlying model. We further demonstrate valve-controlled drainage and use the generated asset library to reproduce laboratory scenes and operations in RoboTwin, supporting reusable simulation environments for robotic laboratory tasks.
2611.33705.why: 实验室设备仿真资产生成

2611.33761.title: ScanAR: Parallel Row-Scan Decoding for Efficient Image Generation in Unified Autoregressive Models
2611.33761.abstract: Unified multimodal autoregressive (AR) models represent text and images in one token sequence and generate all modalities with a shared next-token prediction head. Their image generation, however, decodes an $H\times W$ visual grid token by token in raster order, which takes $HW$ sequential steps and dominates inference time. Existing acceleration methods for visual AR generation either change the tokenizer, the prediction head, or the model interface, or keep the model but cannot reach high parallelism without losing quality, so they do not carry over to unified AR models. We propose ScanAR, a row-scan parallel decoding method that only redefines the predecessors of visual tokens. The first visual row is generated from left to right as usual, and each later row is generated in a single parallel step, with every token predicted from the vertically aligned token of the previous row. Nonvisual tokens keep the standard autoregressive rule. ScanAR reduces the visual decoding depth from $HW$ to $H+W$ without changing the backbone, vocabulary, or output head and without adding parameters, and it supports both training from scratch and lightweight post-training. On Emu3.5-Image-34B, ScanAR post-training reaches a GenEval score of 82.36, the best among post-training acceleration methods trained on the same data, and generates $512\times512$ images $13.8\times$ faster than raster decoding under the same inference setting. On ImageNet, ScanAR trained from scratch has the highest throughput at every model size with FID comparable to raster LlamaGen. On the 34B Xiaomi-Robotics-U0 model, ScanAR preserves the overall quality of embodied scene generation, interleaved image-text generation, and video generation.
2611.33761.why: 自回归图像生成解码加速（AR=autoregressive 误命中）

2611.33792.title: Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology via Topology-Informed Graph Attention and Gene-Semantics Conditioning
2611.33792.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics (ST) profiles gene expression with spatial context but remains costly, motivating models that infer expression from H&E images. Existing approaches face three key limitations: (i) a single patch embedding is often insufficient: morphologically similar regions can exhibit distinct expression due to spatial context, while naive neighborhood aggregation can over-smooth boundaries; (ii) conventional fixed, gene-indexed output heads treat genes independently and cannot directly support strict zero-shot prediction for unseen genes; and (iii) common metrics under-measure spatial pattern fidelity and boundary resolution. To address these challenges, we propose TIGEM, a topology-informed, gene-conditioned framework for histology-to-ST inference. TIGEM learns topology-aware spot representations by regularizing graph attention with tissue-level topology and morphology cues to avoid cross-compartment smoothing, and uses gene semantic modulation to replace gene-indexed heads, enabling zero-shot prediction for unseen genes. We also introduce Graph Spectral Correlation (GSC) to evaluate spatial pattern fidelity and boundary resolution complement to PCC/MSE. Across three large-scale ST datasets, TIGEM achieves overall state-of-the-art performance and significantly improved boundary prediction resolution, and further demonstrates the ability to predict expression patterns for genes unseen during training, extending prior zero-shot histology-to-ST efforts with topology-aware spatial propagation and PLM-based gene conditioning.
2611.33792.why: 空间转录组学预测（计算病理）

2611.33865.title: Measuring the Value of One Shared Image at Robot Handoffs in Vision-and-Language Navigation
2611.33865.abstract: When the lead robot cannot continue, what should it send the teammate that must finish the route? We replay a frozen receiver at each contact under alternative messages. Across 3,920 autonomous departures in 106 environments, adding the view before the lead's last action block to its executed actions raised success by 7.51 percentage points (pp) per RxR handoff and 8.54 pp per SAGE handoff. Per departure the gains were 2.23 and 1.44 pp, respectively. The lead continuing in simulation defines the empirical full-history ceiling (Solo). At contact, the lead had accumulated a median of 41 frames. Sending one frame when available recovered 24% of the full-history advantage over actions alone in SAGE and 30% in RxR. Over an estimated progress cue in SAGE, the image rescued 100 routes and reversed 54 successes. Near-goal receivers finished outside less often (63.1% to 51.7%, post hoc). In secondary comparisons the earlier view outperformed the contact view by 6-7 pp per handoff. Exact-route specificity and image gains at controlled starts with mostly unknown progress or outside the goal region remained unresolved. Gains were detectable from about 7 kB per handoff. Random transmission matched within size bins nearly equaled the learned sender's team success. At a required handoff, a view of the approach to the last maneuver helps the receiver finish.
2611.33865.why: 视觉语言导航机器人接力

2611.33905.title: Tortho-Gaussian++: Suppressing Geometric Drift and Floaters for Robust Gravity-Aligned TDOM Generation in Large-Scale Aerial Scenes
2611.33905.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has demonstrated remarkable performance in aerial scene reconstruction, motivating its recent extension to true digital orthophoto maps (TDOMs) generation. We propose Tortho-Gaussian++, a novel 3DGS training framework that suppresses geometric drift and floaters and automatically prunes unreliable peripheral regions, coupled with a robust gravity-aligned TDOM rendering solution. First, we explore geometric support via viewing-ray-based geometric observability analysis, quantitatively characterizing the reliability for each Gaussian and subsequently pruning peripheral regions with particularly weak geometric support. Second, the optimizer state initialization is refined for newly created Gaussians during densification, intrinsically suppressing drift and floaters without external priors. Lastly, a robust gravity direction estimation solution is designed, combining image-derived gravity cues, camera-distribution priors and nadir views, to achieve a gravity-aligned orthogonal projection reference for TDOM rendering. Extensive experiments on multiple large-scale UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) datasets demonstrate that our Tortho-Gaussian++ outperforms vanilla 3DGS by 0.5-3.5 dB in average PSNR and yields comparable or superior performance to prior-guided 3DGS methods. Notably, it reduces the training time, VRAM and Gaussian number by 45.5%, 47.2%, and 58.6%, respectively. Qualitative evaluations confirm that our method effectively suppresses drift and floaters, while robust gravity direction estimation reduces tilt-induced facade artifacts in TDOMs.
2611.33905.why: 航空 TDOM 正射影像生成（遥感测绘）

2611.33918.title: M\"obiuString: Structured String Art via Optimizing Generatrices on the M\"obius Strip
2611.33918.abstract: String art is a worldwide handicraft that mimics an image with straight strings stretched between boundary pins. Existing image-driven methods primarily optimize individual strings for reconstruction fidelity, leaving the global organization of the strings weakly controlled.In this paper, we introduce the generatrix on the M\"obius strip of unordered boundary-point pairs to formalize families of strings with finite generatrices, enabling explicit control over their arrangement. Based on this new formalization, we propose M\"obiuString, a framework for generating structured, multi-color string art under a prescribed string budget. As an initialization, we place pins along boundaries of image-derived regions and select candidate string segments near each generatrix in the homeomorphic pin-index plane. During the iterative optimization, a 2DGS-based differentiable renderer jointly optimizes generatrix parameters and colors on multiple layers, while periodic discrete re-search revises string families to escape poor local configurations.To our knowledge, M\"obiuString is the first automatic image-based method to generate string art with a structured string organization with freeform region boundaries. Evaluations with two datasets and a user study demonstrate the outperformance of M\"obiuString over baselines.
2611.33918.why: 莫比乌斯带弦艺术生成（计算艺术）

2611.33919.title: DiCALM: Converting Autoregressive Convolution-Attention Language Models into Discrete Diffusion Language Models
2611.33919.abstract: Existing methods for adapting autoregressive (AR) language models to diffusion generation focus mainly on full-attention architectures. More efficient hybrid architectures remain underexplored. We introduce DiCALM, a recipe for converting the hybrid convolution-attention models of the LFM2 family (LFM2 and LFM2.5) from AR to masked-diffusion generation. DiCALM progressively extends LFM2's causal gated convolution so that it captures local context in both directions. It combines this extension with a masking warm-up and joint AR--diffusion training. In controlled experiments, DiCALM performs comparably to the corresponding fine-tuned LFM2.5-based AR models and delivers consistent speedups over them at both the 350M and 1.2B scales: over 1.4x on average and up to 1.79x.
2611.33919.why: 自回归转扩散语言模型（AR=autoregressive 误命中）

2611.33920.title: UPP-Gauss: Ultrasound Propagation Physics-informed Gaussian Splatting for B-mode Novel-View Synthesis
2611.33920.abstract: Accurate novel-view synthesis of B-mode ultrasound images requires modeling acoustic propagation through tissue and the resulting appearance variations across probe poses. We propose Ultrasound Propagation Physics-informed Gaussian Splatting (UPP-Gauss), which integrates these acoustic interactions into an explicit Gaussian representation. UPP-Gauss constructs acoustic maps by sampling three 3D Gaussian fields using the probe pose and acoustic beam propagation direction, then combines these maps according to ultrasound propagation to synthesize B-mode images. Across three acoustically diverse datasets, UPP-Gauss achieves the best reconstruction quality with efficient rendering, improving PSNR over the best baseline on each dataset by 1.43 dB on average. These results demonstrate accurate and efficient B-mode novel-view synthesis through explicit Gaussian modeling of ultrasound propagation.
2611.33920.why: 超声 B 模式高斯泼溅（医学成像）

2611.33934.title: Towards 360$^\circ$ Embodied UAV Tracking Without Turning
2611.33934.abstract: Conventional embodied UAV tracking couples target observability with heading control because targets may leave the field of view of forward-facing cameras. We investigate a complementary paradigm that uses full-spherical perception to follow designated targets without active heading adjustment. To support this setting, we introduce 360UAV-ETrack, a simulation benchmark comprising 2,652 sequences, over 1.73 million synchronized observations, eight tracking tasks, and 150 held-out closed-loop scenarios. We propose 360UAV-TVLA, a panoramic vision--language--action (VLA) framework integrating persistent visual referring (PVR), compressed temporal memory (CTM), and geometry-aligned trajectory supervision (GTS) for instance identification, motion reasoning, and three-dimensional control. Experiments across two VLA backbones show consistent gains over standard fine-tuning, with normalized average tracking frames increasing from 22.56\% to 35.28\% for $\pi_0$ and from 25.68\% to 33.64\% for $\pi_{0.5}$. Our benchmark further reveals a substantial gap between offline imitation accuracy and closed-loop tracking reliability, establishing a challenging testbed for future research https://libingyu01.github.io/360UAV-ETrack_360UAV-TVLA/

2611.33990.title: geo-eval-harness: An Evaluation Harness for Geospatial Foundation Models
2611.33990.abstract: Geospatial foundation model (GFM) research papers are plagued by inconsistent evaluation settings (e.g., different pre-processing and probes), making it difficult to separate performance from evaluation choices. We propose geo-eval-harness}, an open-source framework for controlled model comparisons. We use this harness to evaluate 100 GFMs and general vision models on 6 classification and 14 segmentation datasets, using multiple probes on frozen or low-rank-adapted encoders. We show that under controlled evaluation, general vision backbones are competitive on RGB classification and high-resolution segmentation, but GFMs shine on multispectral tasks. When we compare any two of the top-ten classification models on a single dataset, their 95% confidence intervals overlap 73% of the time. We show that bigger models are not always better: inference FLOPs correlate weakly with segmentation performance. Moreover, translating inference compute into large-area mapping workloads shows how small accuracy differences have outsized deployment cost differences: with frozen encoders on SpaceNet2, a 0.9-point mIoU difference corresponds to 5.9x the compute and days of additional projected GPU time. Our findings stress the importance of comparing models under explicit and fixed settings, and reporting uncertainty and deployment compute alongside accuracy. Our geo-eval-harness makes controlled experiments easy, fast, and fully reproducible. We release the code, configurations, and results at https://github.com/torchgeo/geo-eval-harness.
2611.33990.why: 地理空间基础模型评测框架

2611.33991.title: QK-Bench: Benchmarking Quantitative Kinematic Understanding for Dynamic Spatial Intelligence
2611.33991.abstract: Spatial intelligence concerns both scene structure and its temporal evolution. Yet a semantically correct description can conceal a quantitative error: recognizing that objects are approaching does not determine their closing speed or whether they will meet. Such errors are critical in collision avoidance, trajectory tracking, and reactive grasping, where actions depend on motion magnitude, timing, and relative geometry. We study quantitative kinematic understanding in multimodal large language models (MLLMs): resolving motion magnitude, rate, reference-frame dependence, and future spatial evolution from visual evidence. We introduce the Quantitative Kinematics Benchmark (QK-Bench), comprising 2,341 multiple-choice QA pairs from 379 videos and 17 tasks spanning Object-Centric Kinematics, Camera Ego-Motion Kinematics, and Multi-Object Kinematic Relations. Hidden geometric and temporal signals support trajectory construction and filtering, while fixed kinematic rules map physical quantities to verifiable answers, including categorical labels. Trajectory and question validation ensure target reliability and sufficient visual support in the sampled frames. All models receive a unified monocular RGB input. Evaluations of proprietary, open-source, and spatial MLLMs reveal substantial limitations: the strongest model achieves only 41.2\% overall accuracy, and spatial MLLMs show no consistent advantage. These findings indicate that current advances in spatial intelligence do not reliably transfer to quantitative kinematic understanding.
2611.33991.why: 动态空间智能运动学基准（机器人/具身）

2611.34021.title: Rethinking Unsupervised Cross-Modal Homography Estimation:Spatially Aware Representations and Geometric Consistency Learning
2611.34021.abstract: Unsupervised cross-modal homography estimation is challenging because appearance differences obscure shared geometric structures. Separating modality transfer from homography estimation helps reduce these differences, but accurate alignment still requires effective geometric representations and consistency constraints on the two subtasks. We propose GeoCo (Geometry-Aware and Consistency-Constrained Homography Estimation), a framework that addresses these two requirements without cross-modal transformation labels. Its homography estimator, RVHomo, adapts hierarchical features from a frozen vision foundation model (VFM) and fuses them with local CNN features to capture structural context and spatial detail. Two geometric consistency constraints encourage modality transfer to preserve geometry and homography predictions to remain consistent under synthetic geometric transformations. Through two-stage progressive distillation, we further obtain GeoCo-D, which uses the lightweight RVHomo-D estimator. An intermediate model first learns to perform cross-modal matching without modality transfer, then transfers prediction and feature knowledge to the student, eliminating online VFM extraction. Experiments on GoogleMap, OPT-SAR, FSD, and VIS-IR show that GeoCo reduces mean average corner error by 17.4-46.7% relative to the best-performing baseline on each dataset. GeoCo-D also outperforms all compared baselines while using 98.5% fewer parameters and 70.4% fewer FLOPs than the complete GeoCo teacher.
2611.34021.why: 跨模态单应估计（通用 2D 几何）

2611.34046.title: End-to-End Image-Goal Navigation for Agile Quadrotors via Recurrent State Distillation
2611.34046.abstract: Image-goal navigation asks a robot to reach the viewpoint of a target photograph without a map or goal pose. In three dimensions, this requires not only recognizing the goal but also estimating 3D displacement and generating continuous control actions to approach and settle at the target view. This is difficult because the same visual difference between current and goal image can require very different actions depending on the robot's velocity, yet monocular images alone reveal neither metric scale nor body motion. As a result, existing image-goal policies are limited to planar action spaces and rely on a state estimator for flight control. Policies that map directly from images to low-level control commands have been demonstrated for agile flight, but not toward goal images in unseen environments. We present the first image-goal navigation policy that directly commands thrust and angular rates for agile quadrotor flight in unseen 3D environments, without relying on state estimation (e.g., SLAM, VO, or SfM) or a separate velocity controller. We train a recurrent vision-based policy through a four-stage pipeline that combines geometric and motion supervision with privileged-teacher distillation and end-to-end reinforcement learning fine-tuning. On 1000 held-out flights in unseen environments, the policy achieves an 82.3% success rate with a mean terminal position error of 0.10m across successful flights. Deployed zero-shot on a real quadrotor, the policy reaches an 84% success rate over 25 trials in an unseen indoor environment.

2611.34053.title: xFORM: Accelerating Fixed-Lag LiDAR Odometry with Exact Factor Compression
2611.34053.abstract: Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR) sensors are increasingly popular for state estimation because of their precision, long range, and high measurement rate. Unfortunately, LiDAR Odometry (LO) systems incur substantial computational cost when processing large point clouds, particularly those that jointly refine a window of scan poses. While our prior LO work FORM is real-time, the costs of feature extraction, correspondence search, and the evaluation and linearization of residuals during pose optimization can introduce significant latency. This latency makes downstream tasks such as control and path planning difficult. To overcome this, we present xFORM, which accelerates the three stages of FORM. xFORM uses factor compression to reduce an optimization problem involving hundreds of thousands of feature matches to 34 scalar residuals per scan pair, while preserving the original objective and Gauss-Newton system in exact arithmetic. We integrate this optimizer into two variants: xFORM-CPU, which additionally parallelizes feature extraction on the CPU, and xFORM-GPU, which accelerates feature processing, correspondence search, and factor compression on the GPU. Across fifteen complete sequences from three datasets, xFORM-CPU and xFORM-GPU achieve overall speedups of 1.1-1.4$\times$ and 2.0-4.0$\times$ over FORM, respectively, with no numerically significant differences to the original implementation.
2611.34053.why: LiDAR 里程计因子压缩（激光雷达）

2611.34084.title: TaCo: Rethinking Correlation for Visual Tracking on Edge Devices
2611.34084.abstract: Lightweight trackers have replaced cross-correlation with attention, and on low-power edge hardware they pay for it, since memory-bound softmax, normalization and reshaping operators of attention cost far more time than their arithmetic suggests. Benchmarking efficient trackers on an edge Neural Processing Unit (NPU) and an Arm CPU under one numerically validated protocol, we find that correlation trackers are the fast ones, but they lag in accuracy unless they adopt a ViT backbone, which brings attention back. We revisit what correlation lacks. Template--search interaction serves two roles: conditioning the search features on the target and matching them against it spatially. Attention does both, whereas correlation only matches, and does so on features extracted without knowledge of the target. We present TaCo (Target-aligned Correlation), which supplies the missing conditioning without attention by letting the template enter the per-frame network only as operands computed once per video. A descriptor of the target scales and shifts the search features channel by channel inside the backbone, and kernels aligned with the target box, each with a weight predicted from the template, correlate with them in one matrix product. With the backbone fixed, our correlation remains essential while incurring negligible NPU overhead, offering a better speed-accuracy trade-off than the attention-based interactions we tested. TaCo-T achieves 62.3% LaSOT AUC at 184 FPS on the Rockchip RV1126B NPU and 96 FPS on a Raspberry Pi 5 CPU, 3.0x and 3.5x the NPU speed of HiT-Tiny and AsymTrack-T at higher accuracy. TaCo-B reaches 65.6% at 50 FPS on the NPU, more than twice the speed of HiT-Base, AsymTrack-B and LightFC-vit, again at higher accuracy. Code and models are available at https://github.com/TsingWei/TaCo-Tracker.
2611.34084.why: 边缘设备通用视觉跟踪

2611.34126.title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence?
2611.34126.abstract: In real-world applications like egocentric recording, visual accessibility, and surveillance review, visual evidence for Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) is often only partially captured. A reliable model should match its response to the evidence: answering when sufficient, guessing from visible clues when partial, and abstaining when absent. Yet existing benchmarks enforce a binary answerable-or-unanswerable split, leaving partial evidence unmeasured and obscuring whether failures arise from missing evidence or misjudging sufficiency. We introduce ClueProbe, a diagnostic benchmark to (1) separate perceiving evidence from judging sufficiency, and (2) validate our diagnosis via targeted fine-tuning. ClueProbe comprises 1,721 human-annotated questions across 598 natural videos, labeled Answerable, Guessable, or Unanswerable, alongside controlled perturbations altering wording or visual input. Evaluating 10 open-source and proprietary Video LLMs reveals that failures stem from judgment rather than perception: models perceive the evidence yet lack graded sufficiency awareness, answering or refusing outright while rarely guessing from partial clues. Targeted fine-tuning shows that this reflects missing supervision rather than insufficient capacity: supervising the guess level lifts appropriate guessing from 1.6% to 40.4% without extra false refusals, whereas conventional refusal tuning rejects 92% of guessable questions. Data and code will be released at https://github.com/suat-llm/ClueProbe.
2611.34126.why: 视频 LLM 部分证据作答基准

2611.34133.title: Somatic Alignment: Scaffolding Non-Visible Inner Body Sensations in and beyond Vocal Pedagogy
2611.34133.abstract: Inner bodily sensations inform expressive musical performance but can be difficult to interpret and communicate. Through two separate workshops with five singing learners and four senior voice teachers, we investigate breath control in vocal pedagogy. Participants reported difficulty interpreting bodily sensations (Opacity of Inner Sensations) and translating awareness into intended adjustments (Disconnected Regulation of Inner Sensations), alongside strategies involving touch, demonstration, and imagery. Building on these accounts, we propose the Somatic Alignment Model (SAM), connecting an Intrapersonal Self-Sensing Loop with an Intercorporeal Co-Sensing Loop. SAM examines how external guidance relates to learners' bodily calibration and how interpretive and regulatory authority is negotiated. We articulate three generative design dimensions, Modality, Agency, and Temporality, and illustrate their possible applications in interactive learning systems and first-person soma design inquiries. SAM offers a conceptual lens for supporting bodily awareness and regulation through interaction design.
2611.34133.why: 声乐教学中的内感受 HCI

2611.34240.title: Analemma $\infty$: A Temporal Benchmark for Geospatial Foundation Models
2611.34240.abstract: Satellite time series capture how land surfaces change over time. Pixel-wise temporal foundation models read a year of satellite observations per pixel, yet public benchmarks lack a temporal axis or subsample it to a few dates. We introduce Analemma, a temporal benchmark of six datasets that carry every 10 and 20 m Sentinel-2 band and a time series spanning a growing season, completed where their releases omit geometry, dates, or cloud masks. One frozen-encoder protocol evaluates all models across label ratios and three seeds, with two baselines without pretraining. The TESSERA model ranks first overall. A from-scratch model on monthly composites outranks every foundation model except OlmoEarth v1.3-Base, suggesting that temporal input explains most of the performance. Three evaluation choices left unstated by the source publications each shift TESSERA v1 by 7.6 to 18.6 mIoU, against top-two gaps of 0.6 to 2.8. Data, harness and leaderboard will be publicly released soon.

2611.34257.title: CamAct: Learning Robotic Manipulation from In-the-Wild Videos via Camera Motion
2611.34257.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models benefit from large, diverse datasets for robotic manipulation, yet collecting robot demonstrations remains costly. Recent work has explored egocentric videos as a source of supervision, primarily drawing on demonstrations of human-object interaction. We show that in-the-wild videos can improve robotic manipulation even when they contain no demonstrations of object manipulation. Specifically, camera motion recovered from these videos provides an additional source of motion supervision that complements robot demonstrations. Building on this finding, we introduce CamAct, which incorporates this camera-motion supervision into VLA policies alongside robot demonstrations, extending the use of human videos for manipulation learning beyond object interactions. Experiments show that incorporating this video supervision during fine-tuning improves success rates from 96.40% to 98.10% on LIBERO and from 22.96% to 29.32% on RoboCasa 365. The resulting policy also demonstrates strong results in out-of-distribution generalization on LIBERO-Plus and real-world manipulation tasks.
2611.34257.why: 相机运动驱动的机器人操作学习

2611.34298.title: RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations
